parts.note: Shaw's one-act play The Shewing-up of ... is subtitled 'A sermon in crude melodrama'; the hero, a horse thief, is shown up and then cleared at his trial, and his surname suggests whitening

clue.text: "O — Envy! thou self-tormenting fiend" (Tobias Smollett, Peregrine Pickle)

clue.text: Grey character in Bronte novel

explanation.definitionFit: Anne Bronte's governess heroine has this first name and the surname Grey, which is also the novel's title.

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the soldier in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience and to the Victorian parodist of Cambridge fame.

explanation.walkthrough: 'still' reads as 'even now' at the end of the sentence; it is the definition, meaning motionless.

clue.text: Inaccurate description of fiction?

clue.text: Typical Elizabethan exhibiting mood swings?
